scope: Schweiz · Zivil- und Strafverfahren, elektronische Signaturen

expert_role.basis: ZPO Art. 183: the court may obtain an expert opinion on a party's request or of its own motion after hearing the parties; the grounds for recusal of court officers apply.

esig_regulation.basis: ZertES (SR 943.03) Art. 2 defines electronic, advanced and qualified electronic signatures and the qualified electronic time stamp. OR Art. 14 Abs. 2bis: a qualified electronic signature combined with a qualified time stamp is equivalent to a handwritten signature, subject to other statutory or agreed rules.

data_access_basis.basis: Processing that infringes personality is unlawful unless justified by consent, an overriding private or public interest, or law (Art. 31(1)).

timestamp_recognition.basis: ZertES Art. 2 lit. j: a qualified electronic time stamp is issued by a provider recognised under ZertES and bears a regulated electronic seal. OR Art. 14 Abs. 2bis links signature equivalence to a qualified time stamp. No statutory presumption for time stamps comparable to eIDAS Art. 41(2) was identified in these provisions.

evidence_rules.basis: The court forms its conviction by free evaluation of the evidence. Unlawfully obtained evidence is considered only if the interest in finding the truth prevails.
Documents include electronic files, photos and recordings. A document may be filed as a copy; the original or a certified copy can be required where there are reasonable doubts about authenticity.
The court evaluates evidence freely according to its conviction from the whole proceedings. Authorities use all legally admissible evidence suited to finding the truth.

Evidence obtained by prohibited methods is never usable. Evidence obtained by authorities through criminal acts or in breach of validity rules is usable only where indispensable to solve serious offences.

dpa.name: Eidgenössischer Datenschutz- und Öffentlichkeitsbeauftragter (EDÖB)
dpa.name_en: Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner
